requirement:
The harness MUST expose a `references` tool with this interface:

```text
references({ selection: String? }) -> ReferenceIndex

ReferenceIndex {
    definitions: Array<DefinitionName>,
    sites: Array<ReferenceSite>,
}

DefinitionName { name: String, kind: "requirement" | "example" }

ReferenceSite {
    name: String,
    role: "impl" | "cite" | "test",
    file: String,
    item: String?,
}
```

`selection` MUST be a {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`.
Without `selection`, the tool MUST return
the full name and kind of every requirement and named example in full-name
order, with empty `sites`. With `selection`, it MUST return the selected definitions
in full-name order and one flattened `sites` array containing every valid
`{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` reference to any match under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, each naming the definition it
references, ordered by name, file, and position in the file, without line
numbers. An anchor under {cite}`requirements.references.anchors` MUST be
reported as a site for its anchored file, with the anchored node's selector as
`item` when it names one and no `item` when it names the whole file. Every
other site MUST give as `item` the selector of its smallest enclosing outline
node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`. Only sources reference discovery considers under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery` MUST contribute sites. If reading such a
source fails, the tool MUST return an explanatory tool error naming the source.
An invalid selection or one matching no definition MUST return an explanatory tool
error.

Results are listings without source text. Like directory listings, they MUST
NOT become evidence inputs; the model requests the sources it relies on with the
`habeas` tool.
rationale:
I found no gap against `requirements.authoring.reference_index`. Every obligation maps to code reachable from the marked `{impl}` items and has a test that runs it and asserts the outcome.

**Interface.**
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[definitions]` advertises a `references` tool with an optional string `selection` and `additionalProperties: false`.
- `references_tool_is_advertised_with_an_optional_selection` asserts the schema and the description wording.
- `fn[dispatch_paged]` routes `"references"` to `fn[references]`. `const[REFERENCE_ARRAYS]` fixes the result shape as `definitions` then `sites`.

**Selection and definitions.**
- `fn[references]` rejects unknown keys and non-string selections. It validates the selection with `definition_glob::validate`.
- It selects requirements and examples, excluding terms, and emits `{name, kind}` in the order `load_definitions` returns them. `references_list_names_and_flattened_sites_without_recording_inputs` asserts this order.
- Without `selection`, it returns the definitions and an empty `sites` array. The test asserts this exact output.
- An invalid selection (`"bad name"`, `""`, `1`) or one matching no definition (`"requirements.missing"`) returns an error, and the test covers each case.
- A selection that matches no definition returns the "matches no requirement or named example" error.

**Sites.**
- `fn[references]` calls `collect_references`, which is the discovery path. It keeps only `Impl`, `Cite` and `Test` references that are closed, match the selection, and name a non-term definition.
- Each site gets its `item` from `owner_at_line`, which is the smallest enclosing outline node. This follows the comment-run rule for fenced and nested comments, and `references_list_names_and_flattened_sites_without_recording_inputs` exercises both.
- Anchors are added as sites with `item` set to the anchored selector, or `null` for a whole file. Anchors to sources access does not permit are skipped. `references_report_anchors_as_file_or_node_sites` asserts this.
- Sites are sorted by name, then file, then line. Anchors have no line, so `None` sorts before any line number. The results carry no line numbers.
- `{fixme}` references and unclosed fences are not sites. The test covers both.

**Sources considered.** `references_report_only_sites_in_considered_sources` shows that sites from files outside the Git index or under `evidence.disallow` are omitted. This relies on `collect_references`, which `requirements.references.discovery` governs.

**Read failures.** If any considered source can't be read, `collect_references` fills `errors` and `references` returns an error naming that source. `references_name_a_considered_source_that_cannot_be_read` asserts the message contains the file path.

**No evidence inputs.** The `Listing` result carries no inputs. The tests assert `inputs.is_empty()`.

**Paging.** `reference_results_page_definitions_then_sites` verifies that definitions are delivered before sites across pages, with no inputs.

I found no behaviour in the implementation that the requirement or the cited requirements don't specify.

in full-name order and one flattened `sites` array containing every valid

:::{req} discovery
Habeas MUST find the references of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`
in project source files, where {cite}`requirements.references.reference_contexts`
says they count, and MUST fail with the source file and line if a
name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped
roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Reference discovery MUST
consider exactly the project sources that source-access policy permits under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`: in a Git worktree, files present in
the Git index, including staged new files; outside Git, all project files; in
both cases excluding the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories, `.git`
and `target` directories at any depth, and paths disallowed by
{cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`. Evidence snapshots and
generated build output MUST therefore not be counted as source references.
:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
An anchored file or node MUST be covered by the definition's evidence under
{cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`, by an input selecting it, so changing the file makes that evidence stale. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference, because the
definition cannot be assessed without it. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such
as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the
definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
